title: Elementary submodels: Tarski–Vaught and Löwenheim–Skolem

based_on.title: Model Theory Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 6–7 (function closure, generated substructures and embeddings); 33–34 (Propositions 4.1–4.2 and elementary embeddings); notes dated 2018-12-14

summary: Describe the substructure generated by parameters, distinguish embeddings from elementary maps, and construct small elementary submodels using witnesses.
abstract: A subset of a structure must retain its constants and remain closed under its functions before it can carry the same operations. Starting with chosen parameters, we describe the smallest such carrier by the values of terms, including the possibility of an empty carrier when neither parameters nor constants are present. An embedding preserves all quantifier-free facts, while an elementary embedding also preserves statements that ask for witnesses elsewhere in the domain. The Tarski–Vaught criterion identifies exactly which substructures retain those witnesses. Repeatedly adjoining them constructs elementary submodels containing any prescribed parameters, with a countable domain in a countable language and a general cardinality bound.
